newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cigarette plant to cut jobs.
newsitem.headline: Polish cigarette plant to cut jobs.

text.p: German tobacco company Reemtsma GmbH plans to cut 10 percent of jobs at its Polish plant WWT SA due to shrinking demand for cigarettes in Poland, WTT president Krzysztof Wagrodzki said on Monday.
PAP news agency quoted Wagrowski as saying that the expected lower demand forced his company to cut production targets for 1996 and dismiss about 250 workers by the end of the year. @
"Only 90 billion cigarettes are forecast to be sold in our country this year as a result their price growth, which is due to an increase in the excise tax on tobacco," he was quoted as saying.
In 1995, cigarettes sales in Poland reached nearly 96 billion. But an increase of the excise tax in April pushed cigarette prices up by between three and five percent and curbed demand.
Wagrodzki said WTT, based in the western city of Poznan was likely to produce 25.5 billion cigarettes in 1996, seven percent less than last year. @
He complained that tobacco makers had been hit by cigarette smuggling, especially from the former Soviet countries, which could amount to eight billion cigarettes next year.
WTT, in which Reemtsma holds a 76 percent stake, controls about 27 percent of Poland's cigarette market.
It is one of five western tobacco companies which last year took part in the privatisation of Poland's tobacco industry.
Other companies are Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co from the United States, French Seita and British American Tobacco Industries Plc. @
Poland's tobacco excise tax is now between 40.3 zloty and 58.3 zloyts per 1,000 cigarettes, depending on their type.
